measurementSource: Original private PromptSnapshots before home-path redaction; raw file unchanged. Public receipt contains the same recorded numeric measurements but redacted text.
method: Unicode character counts of the two message contents in each of16 main PromptSnapshots, excluding JSON envelope syntax. These shares are not tokenizer attribution. Provider usage is reported separately.

checkPayload.note: Repeated appearances across input snapshots include inherited prior-run history. These counts are not unique tool invocations.

redundantCurrentRunAttempts.explanation: Seven calls repeated the same already-failed assertion plan after its first failure. They are model attempts, not transport retries or parse repairs.
redundantCurrentRunAttempts.note: Observed expenditure, not a guaranteed counterfactual saving; a corrected recovery still needs inference and checks.

compaction.outcome: All three completed and were adopted. Lowering the compaction threshold is not justified by this one run.

recommendationOrder: Keep typed workspace failures and bounded captured-native expected/actual diagnostics.
Project workspace_check receipts for model input while retaining full immutable check proof and exact event records separately.
Use stage/call references in opt-in model observation history instead of echoing arguments already present in the assistant action.
Only then evaluate smaller workbench instructions or unused capability grants using matched settings. Do not add generic repeat denial or mutable-tool caching.

offlineCheckProjection.method: Current scoped builtin validator/projector and staged-v1 serializer, fed nine original recorded check receipts without model or browser execution. Synthetic call IDs reconstructed from recorded request and call order. Historical records unchanged.
offlineCheckProjection.scope: Only the nine workspace_check observation blocks. This excludes unchanged assistant plans, generic result escaping, repeated appearances in later prompts, added format instructions, and tokenization. No end-to-end latency or model reliability claim.
